column1:
- Policy stance: The Committee delivered a 25 bp hike to 4.50–4.75% and reiterated “ongoing increases,” continued balance sheet runoff, and firm control of short rates via IORB at 4.65% and ON RRP at 4.55%—still a moderately hawkish posture focused on returning inflation to 2%.
- Beige Book overlay (Jan 2023): District reports described overall activity as flat to slightly down, with consumers increasingly price sensitive and mixed holiday spending; manufacturing generally flat or softer; housing and CRE weak. Labor markets remained tight but showed easing labor shortages and moderating wage growth. Price increases continued to slow in many Districts, though inflation remained elevated. Outlooks were described as more uncertain and cautious.
- SLOOS overlay: Broad-based tightening in bank lending standards and softer loan demand for C&I and CRE, with firms citing reduced financing needs across capex, M&A, inventories, and receivables.
- Implications: Beige Book moderation in activity, easing wage pressures, and slowing price gains—together with SLOOS-driven endogenous tightening—reinforce the Committee’s emphasis on cumulative tightening and policy lags, reducing the need for an aggressively hawkish path from here.
- Net: Still a hawkish bias due to elevated inflation and ongoing hikes, but Beige Book and SLOOS developments temper the stance closer to neutral.
